title: Three-notes-per-string scales
description: 3NPS as a seven-note grid: how it is built, what overlaps, and what it leaves out.

cards.front: What is three notes per string (3NPS)?
cards.back: A way to organize a seven-note scale so each string carries exactly three consecutive scale notes. Six strings give 18 notes — about two and a half octaves.

cards.front: Is 3NPS a theory of which notes to play?
cards.back: No. It is an organizational tool: a consistent grid you can pick evenly and slide between. It does not show chords or the key.
Deal scale notes onto the strings from string 6 up, three per string. Start on a different degree on the lowest string and you get a different position. Seven starting degrees, seven patterns.

cards.front: Why aren’t the seven 3NPS shapes interchangeable copies?
cards.back: Most strings are a fourth (5 frets) apart; G to B is a major third (4 frets). That changes the fret shape on strings 3 and 2.

cards.front: C major 3NPS starting on G (frets 3–8): notes and frets per string.
C major 3NPS starting on A (frets 5–10): notes and frets per string.

cards.back: Each string drops its first note and adds the next scale note, so the two positions share two notes per string. On string 6, A B (frets 5 and 7) belong to both the G and A positions.

cards.front: Why organize by three notes per string?
cards.back: Even picking and legato, a five-to-six-fret hand span, and two-note overlaps for sliding into the next position.
No. A five-note scale does not divide into threes; pentatonic patterns use two notes per string. Other seven-note scales get their own 3NPS grids built the same way.

cards.front: Build the C major position starting on C (string 6 fret 8).
Build 3NPS starting on G in G major (has F♯). What changed vs C major’s G position?
cards.back: 6 G A B 3 5 7. 5 C D E 3 5 7. 4 F♯ G A 4 5 7. 3 B C D 4 5 7. 2 E F♯ G 5 7 8. 1 A B C 5 7 8. F became F♯ on strings 4 and 2 (up one fret).

cards.front: In the A position of C major, where do you pass C?
cards.back: String 6 fret 8, string 3 fret 5, string 1 fret 8.

cards.front: In the G position of C major, where is the root C?
cards.back: String 5 fret 3, string 3 fret 5, string 1 fret 8.

cards.front: Which CAGED C shapes sit inside the G-position 3NPS box (frets 3–8)?
cards.back: A-shape C (x35553) and G-shape C (875558). Chord tones inside the grid: 5/3 C, 5/7 E, 4/5 G.

cards.front: Does the 3NPS grid itself decide whether a run sounds like C major or A minor?
cards.back: No. That depends on where you start, where you land, and which notes you stress against the chord.
